summary: APIGW routed websocket streaming connections to batch handler, causing serving-runtime overload and sustained 5xx
description: Multiple customers reported a sudden spike in 5xx responses beginning ~2026-03-10 02:12 UTC. High-rate streaming clients (websocket based) experienced disconnects and immediate 5xx responses. Metrics show sustained error-rate increase on several ingress nodes and correlated serving-runtime OOMs and restart cycles. Initial symptom: high CPU and memory on downstream batch route workers followed by process exits and upstream 502/503s. Customer payloads were streaming chat sessions but were being routed to a route configured for large, synchronous batch embedding jobs (batch handler), causing long-lived websocket sessions to occupy batch worker slots and trigger KV/prefetch lock contention and eventual OOMs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Establish a websocket streaming session that sends small chat deltas every 50-200ms. 2) Observe topology: some sessions were incorrectly routed to /v1/batch/embed handler instead of /v1/stream/chat. 3) Under concurrent load (~500 concurrent streaming sessions) the misrouted batch workers accumulate many half-open streams, holding memory and prefetch resources. 4) After ~2-5 minutes, serving-runtime reports OOM and restarts; API gateway surfaces 502/503 to callers.
logs:
- apigw logs (us-east-1) show route rewrite: original_path=/v1/stream/chat, rewritten_path=/v1/batch/embed, reason=route-set-by-priority (2026-03-10T02:11:58Z)
- runtime stderr: 'Allocation failed: device out of memory' (2026-03-10T02:14:05Z)
- runtime supervisor: restart_count=3 within 2m (2026-03-10T02:16:20Z)
- metrics: error_rate(api_gateway)=12% (baseline 0.2%), pod_restarts(serving-runtime)=7 in 10m
- tcp traces: many KEEPALIVE half-open sockets to batch-handler backends, long time_waits
investigation_notes:
- Noticed a rewrite rule introduced in latest ingress ruleset (PR #gh-5721) that tightened route priority ordering. The rule deprioritized the streaming prefix in some edge nodes, allowing a catch-all batch route to match first.
- Correlated runtime OOM stack traces show cumulative KV cache growth with many small streams holding pointers; batch handler expects bulk upload patterns and delays releasing memory for streaming frames.
- Reproduction done in staging by replaying websocket traffic to batch endpoint -> reproduces leak within 3 minutes.
- Hypothesis: route priority change + difference in connection handling semantics between batch and streaming handlers produced sustained resource retention, amplifying under burst and leading to process OOMs.
- Customer impact: TextFlow reported ~40% of active streams dropped; affects dedicated cluster customers using streaming chat concurrently with batch embedding jobs.
timeline:
2026-03-10 02:11 UTC - First alert from TextFlow about increased 5xx
2026-03-10 02:12 UTC - Pager triggered, on-call acknowledged
2026-03-10 02:14 UTC - Observed runtime OOMs and restarts in affected pods
2026-03-10 02:20 UTC - Identified suspicious route rewrite behavior; rolled routing change to previous policy on a subset of edge nodes
2026-03-10 02:27 UTC - Error rate on nodes where rollback applied fell back to baseline
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC - Full rollback of the ingress priority change completed; monitoring shows steady decline in 5xx and no further OOMs
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Customer verified stream stability and resumed normal traffic
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10T02:13Z: Customer TextFlow reports large number of dropped streaming sessions and 5xx. Collected request ids and sample websocket traces.
SRE (Arjun Patel) 2026-03-10T02:18Z: Seeing OOMs on batch-handler pods; correlating with apigw rewrite logs. Rolling partial ingress rollback to test.
SRE (Nina Alvarez) 2026-03-10T02:26Z: Partial rollback reduced error-rate on subset of nodes. Staging replay confirms misroute causes resource retention in batch handler.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10T02:45Z: Informed TextFlow of temporary routing rollback and asked for validation. Customer confirms streams restored.

Engineering (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-11T10:12Z: Created follow-up engineering task to add additional route-validation unit tests and to harden batch handler to close streaming connections early and fail fast when unexpected protocol is detected. See GH #gh-5739.
Customer (TextFlow - Priya Rao) 2026-03-10T03:20Z: Thanks for quick rollback; we'll hold off on heavy streaming jobs for the next 24h while you root cause and patch.
resolution: Mitigated by rolling back ingress priority change at 2026-03-10T02:40Z which stopped misrouting websocket streams to the batch handler. Applied short-term patch to apigw to detect streaming websocket handshake on batch routes and reject with 4xx instead of forwarding. No code changes to serving-runtime required for mitigation; long-term fixes planned.
root_cause: Ingress route priority change (GH-5721) caused a catch-all batch route to match websocket streaming sessions on some edge nodes. Batch handler connection semantics retained streaming frames, causing resource retention and runtime OOMs under load.
next_steps:
1) Engineering to land GH-5739: add route-matching unit tests and enforce explicit websocket/non-websocket route annotations (ETA 2026-03-14).
2) Harden batch handler to detect websocket handshakes and reject early (PR opened).
3) Add monitoring alert for 'route-rewrite-to-batch-with-websocket-handshake' to detect regressions.
4) Run targeted chaos test in staging to validate route-priority changes before rollout.
5) Follow-up customer communication: postmortem and RCA in Confluence (by 2026-03-15).
